tasks.title: Implement MV3 agent command bridge, trusted sessions, and audit envelope
tasks.description: Add the background-owned command bridge that accepts JSON command envelopes through the existing localhost webService transport, validates Trusted Agent Mode capabilities, executes routed commands, and returns the standard response envelope.
tasks.details: Build on existing MV3 surfaces: src/manifest.chrome*.json already registers webService.bundle.js on localhost, src/content/services/webService.js already proxies localhost page events, and src/background/index.js already owns runtime message handling through MessageListener. Add bridge modules such as src/agentBridge/background/router.js, capabilities.js, audit.js, and errors.js, then register a background listener like message.on('agent:command', async envelope => handleAgentCommand(envelope)). Extend webService to listen for a dedicated bridge event from the CLI bridge page and forward it to background via sendMessage('agent:command', envelope, 'background'). Persist one-time setup token and capability config in browser.storage.local, but keep per-session state in memory. Pseudo-code: parse envelope -> require id/command/payload -> resolve required capabilities by command -> compare against trusted session capability set -> return { ok:false, errors:[{ code:'missing_capability', capability }] } on denial -> execute handler -> write audit event with redacted payload summary -> return { ok:true, data, warnings:[], errors:[], auditId }. Redact cookies, secrets, uploaded file contents, huge tables/logs, and raw page data by default; support verbose audit mode only through explicit trusted config. Follow Chrome MV3 JSON-serializable runtime messaging constraints and service worker ownership model documented at https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/messaging and https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/service-workers.
tasks.testStrategy: Use node --test for pure router, capability, envelope, and audit-redaction modules with mocked storage and handlers. Add cases for malformed envelopes, missing capabilities, trusted no-prompt command execution, standard success/error envelopes, audit id generation, and redaction. Manually verify a localhost bridge page can send a command through webService.bundle.js and receive a background response in Chrome MV3.

Add src/agentBridge/background/router.test.js covering malformed input, missing id/command, unknown command lookup, thrown async/sync handlers, successful dispatch, and stable { ok, id, data, warnings, errors } response shape. subtasks.title: Implement command router with capability lookup and handler dispatch
subtasks.description: Route validated command envelopes to registered handlers after resolving required capabilities.
subtasks.details:
Build a handler registry in router.js with command-to-capability metadata. Implement handleAgentCommand(envelope, context) as the single background entry point: parse envelope, resolve required capabilities, call capability checks, execute the handler, attach auditId, and return standard envelopes. Stub initial handlers or support injected handlers for tests until later tasks add real commands.
<info added on 2026-06-29T18:10:35.504Z>
Add src/agentBridge/background/router.js as a pure module using the existing @ alias/ES module style. Model the registry as command metadata plus async handler functions, with a registerAgentCommand helper for test injection and a default registry that can start with no-op/placeholder handlers until Task 4 adds workflow.* implementations. Wire src/background/index.js to import handleAgentCommand and register message.on('agent:command', (envelope, sender) => handleAgentCommand(envelope, { sender, browser, now: Date.now })) alongside existing background-prefixed MessageListener handlers. The router should call the envelope parser/helpers from Subtask 1.1 first, derive required capabilities from the registry entry, delegate authorization to src/agentBridge/background/capabilities.js, create success/failure audit records through audit.js with command, capability list, session/trust metadata, and error code, then return the standard response envelope with auditId attached. Normalize handler output through a JSON-safe serializer such as JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value ?? null)) before returning because responses cross browser.runtime messaging and the localhost webService bridge. Map unknown commands, malformed envelopes, denied capabilities, and handler exceptions through errors.js so callers receive consistent error envelopes and audit failures are still recorded. Include node --test coverage for registry lookup, injected handlers, async dispatch, capability denial short-circuiting, unknown command errors, auditId propagation, and non-serializable handler results.
</info added on 2026-06-29T18:10:35.504Z>
subtasks.testStrategy: Use node --test with mocked handlers for successful dispatch, unknown command rejection, capability denial propagation, async handler behavior, and JSON-safe response data.

subtasks.title: Add trusted session and capability storage module
subtasks.description: Persist trusted configuration in browser.storage.local while keeping active trusted sessions in memory.

Maintain per-session trust and capability grants in service-worker memory. Expose helpers to create, validate, and clear trusted sessions, and to compare required command capabilities against the active session capability set.
<info added on 2026-06-29T18:11:15.765Z>
Use the project’s existing ES module and storage style: import browser from webextension-polyfill as in src/background/index.js and use browser.storage.local.get/set with explicit keys like src/stores/workflow.js and src/content/services/webService.js. Keep src/agentBridge/background/capabilities.js as a pure background-side module, independent of the localhost content webService script, so the future background MessageListener agent:command handler can call it. Persist one agentBridgeTrustedConfig object containing setupToken, trusted clients/origins, allowedCapabilities, updatedAt, and optional tokenConsumedAt, defaulting missing storage to a locked-down config. Track active trust in a module-scoped Map keyed by a generated sessionId with grantedCapabilities as a Set plus origin/client metadata, createdAt, expiresAt, and lastUsedAt so MV3 service-worker restarts drop trust. Export helpers for load/save/clear config, setup token set/consume, create/validate/clear sessions, clearing all sessions, normalizing capability lists, and checking required capabilities. Capability checks should accept router command requirements as a string or array, treat missing requirements as allowed only for explicitly public commands, and return structured allow/deny data for the router/errors modules rather than throwing storage-specific errors.
</info added on 2026-06-29T18:11:15.765Z>

tasks.title: Add block catalog schema generation and structured validation
tasks.description: Generate code-first block schemas from existing Automa block definitions and normalize validation errors for agent correction.
tasks.details: Use src/utils/shared.js tasks as the primary block catalog source, including built-in entries such as trigger, new-tab, conditions, and ai-workflow. Include custom/saved blocks from the same getBlocks/catalog path used by the UI if present, and derive schema fields from task.data defaults, task.inputs, task.outputs, category, component, maxConnection, and allowedInputs. Adapt src/newtab/utils/blocksValidation.js validators into a structured validator layer that returns stable objects such as { code, path, message, severity, blockId, alias }. Infer primitive parameter types from defaults and keep unknown/custom block data blocked in strict mode unless unsafeRaw:true is supplied. Treat ai-workflow as a normal catalog entry only; do not add creation or management of AI Power workflows. Pseudo-code: listSchemas() => Object.entries(tasks).map(toBlockSchema); getSchema(type) => schema or unknown_block; validateBlock(type,data,{unsafeRaw}) => merge defaults -> run known validator -> normalize string errors -> return { errors,warnings,normalizedData }.
tasks.testStrategy: Add node --test coverage for schema generation of new-tab, trigger, conditions, and ai-workflow; default extraction; input/output connection shapes; unknown block rejection; unsafeRaw acceptance; duplicate/missing/invalid parameter error normalization; and preservation of warning versus blocking error semantics. Run npm run lint and npm run build after integration.

subtasks.details:
When a type is missing from the known catalog, return an unknown_block schema marker and reject validation in strict mode with a structured error unless unsafeRaw:true is supplied. For custom or saved blocks discovered through the UI catalog path, include their schema when enough metadata exists; otherwise mark unsafe or unknown fields explicitly. When unsafeRaw:true is supplied, accept raw data without applying unknown validators while still returning stable warnings where appropriate.

If a workflow node label/type is absent from that map, emit a schema descriptor with kind/type unknown_block, preserve the original label for diagnostics, and make strict validation return a blocking structured error such as unknown_block_type unless options.unsafeRaw is true. Treat saved package nodes from src/newtab/pages/workflows/[id].vue, including label block-package and savedBlocks data where settings.asBlock controls package-as-block behavior, and custom blocks from business/dev/blocks/index.js as unsafe when they lack enough task metadata to derive data defaults, inputs, outputs, component, allowedInputs, or maxConnection. Strict mode should reject those cases with stable unsafe_custom_block or unsafe_saved_block errors. With unsafeRaw:true, bypass per-field unknown validators and accept raw node data while still attaching deterministic warnings for unknown_block, unsafe_custom_block, or unsafe_saved_block.

tasks.title: Implement Workflow Outline conversion, alias metadata, draft mutations, and concurrency checks
tasks.description: Create the agent-facing Workflow Outline model and in-memory draft authoring operations while preserving Automa drawflow storage and UI compatibility.
tasks.details: Add pure workflow-model modules for converting Automa drawflow to outlines and back without replacing node ids. Reuse existing drawflow shape from src/stores/workflow.js and src/utils/convertWorkflowData.js: workflows store nodes/edges, trigger defaults, settings, updatedAt, and browser.storage.local persistence. Persist block aliases under workflow.settings metadata keyed by internal node id, for example settings.agentBridge.aliases[nodeId] = alias. Implement beginDraft, addBlock, updateBlock, removeBlock, connectBlocks, disconnectBlocks, appendBlock, insertBlock, validate, diffDraft, commitDraft, and discardDraft in an in-memory draft manager owned by background. beginDraft records baseRevision from updatedAt or a content hash; commitDraft refetches the live workflow from browser.storage.local and rejects with workflow_conflict if changed. Duplicate aliases are rejected in strict mode. Connection helpers must preserve explicit output handles, conditions branches, fallback outputs, and multi-output blocks. Layout should preserve existing positions and deterministically place new blocks near the logical source with collision avoidance. Pseudo-code: beginDraft(id) -> live=store.get(id), draft=clone(live), rev=revision(live); addBlock(draftId,type,{alias,params}) -> schema validate -> node={id:nanoid(),label:type,type:tasks[type].component,data:merge(defaults,params),position:layout(...)} -> aliases[id]=alias; connectBlocks(sourceAlias,targetAlias,handle='1') -> add vueflow edge; commitDraft -> if revision(live)!=baseRev return conflict -> write drawflow/settings/updatedAt -> register trigger when needed.
tasks.testStrategy: Use node --test for drawflow-to-outline conversion, outline-to-drawflow preservation, alias persistence, duplicate alias rejection, add/update/remove/connect operations, append/insert helpers, linear and multi-output connection creation, deterministic non-overlapping layout, draft isolation from live workflow, diff summaries, and optimistic concurrency conflict. Add a fixture using workflows/chatgpt-deep-research.automa.json and a minimal generated workflow to confirm existing UI-compatible drawflow remains valid.

Add revision(liveWorkflow) that prefers updatedAt and falls back to a deterministic content hash for optimistic concurrency.

Define helpers for stable JSON normalization and revision hashing that ignore object insertion order and preserve array order for drawflow.nodes and drawflow.edges, matching the VueFlow shape used by src/stores/workflow.js and src/utils/convertWorkflowData.js. Add outline block records from node fields id, label, type, data, position, plus connection records from edge fields id, source, target, sourceHandle, and targetHandle. Add alias metadata helpers for workflow.settings.agentBridge.aliases keyed by node id, including get/set/delete normalization without overwriting unrelated workflow.settings values. Add validation primitives shared by conversion and drafts: plain-object checks, required node/edge field checks, node id existence checks for edge endpoints, duplicate alias detection, missing trigger detection, and handle parsing for output names such as output-1, output-fallback, and condition ids.
</info added on 2026-06-29T18:48:38.124Z>

Support conditions branches, fallback outputs, and multi-output block handles. appendBlock should add and connect after a logical source. insertBlock should splice a block between existing source and target connections.

Position appended or inserted blocks near the source node using consistent offsets, scan for occupied coordinates, and avoid collisions without relying on random ordering.

subtasks.details: On commitDraft, refetch the live workflow from browser.storage.local, recompute revision, and reject with workflow_conflict if it differs from baseRevision. On success, convert the draft back to drawflow, update settings and updatedAt, persist the workflow, and register triggers when workflow changes require it.

tasks.description: Wire command handlers for workflow read/write/storage operations and runtime execution/log inspection against the installed extension workflow store and existing Automa engine.
tasks.details: Implement command handlers for workflow.list, workflow.getOutline, workflow.getRaw, workflow.create, workflow.replace, workflow.delete, workflow.run, workflow.stop, workflow.getRunState, workflow.getLogs, workflow.getLogDetail, and workflow.getTable. Reuse BackgroundWorkflowUtils/WorkflowManager execution paths already exposed in src/background/index.js for workflow:execute, workflow:stop, workflow:resume, and workflow state storage. Read bounded runtime data from existing Dexie logs schema in src/db/logs.js: items, histories, ctxData, and logsData. Enforce defaults from the PRD: latest 20 log summaries, one selected log detail, first 100 table rows with cursor/pagination when practical. Pseudo-code: workflow.run(id) -> require workflow:run -> workflow=store.get(id) -> BackgroundWorkflowUtils.instance.executeWorkflow(workflow,{}) -> return run state id if available; getLogs(id,{limit=20}) -> clamp limit -> dbLogs.items.where('workflowId').equals(id).reverseBy('endedAt').limit(limit); getLogDetail(logId) -> fetch item/history/ctx/logsData; getTable(id,{limit=100,cursor}) -> return rows slice + nextCursor.

tasks.title: Add automa-agent CLI, bridge server lifecycle, and end-to-end verification
tasks.description: Provide the npm bin and shell-facing commands that start a local bridge server, open the bridge page, wait for extension handshake, send JSON commands, and expose workflow/block subcommands.
tasks.details: Add package.json bin { "automa-agent": "bin/automa-agent.mjs" } and implement bin/automa-agent.mjs as a thin CLI over the JSON command protocol, not as the authoritative API. Use Node built-ins where possible for argument parsing, localhost HTTP server, and command dispatch; keep dependencies minimal because the project already uses Webpack and Node scripts. The CLI should implement the examples from the PRD: bridge start --trusted --token <token>, workflow list/get/begin-draft/add-block/connect/validate/commit/run/logs, and blocks list/schema/search. bridge start should launch a localhost server, serve a small bridge page, open it in Chrome, wait for the webService/extension handshake, then send queued JSON envelopes and print bounded JSON responses. Support --param key=value parsing, --format outline, --limit, trusted token injection, nonzero exit codes for structured errors, and redacted logs. Add a test script such as "test": "node --test" while preserving existing relay:test. Pseudo-code: parse argv -> commandSpec -> envelope={id,command,capabilities,payload} -> bridgeClient.send(envelope) -> if !ok print JSON to stderr and exit 1 else print data/envelope JSON. Current Node test runner reference: https://nodejs.org/api/test.html.
tasks.testStrategy: Use node --test for CLI argv parsing, --param coercion, command-to-envelope mapping, response handling, structured error exit behavior, bridge handshake timeout, token/capability propagation, and JSON output stability. Run npm run lint, npm run build, and node --test. Complete the manual acceptance scenario: start Chrome MV3 dev extension, run automa-agent bridge start --trusted, fetch workflows, create a draft, add new-tab and get-text blocks, commit, run, fetch latest logs, and confirm Trusted Agent Mode never prompts between commands.
